input: SC-LU-TRUNKS-001 — Lineup decode: Future Trunks, 'The Future That Never Arrived'. Travels back from a ruined future to change the past; the timeline he saves is not his own; his own future is later erased by Future Zeno. A successful intervention that leaves the intervener outside the world it fixed.

metadata.title: Lineup Decode: Future Trunks — The Future That Never Arrived

addenda.note: RUL-BINARY-001 rev 2 (Shax t571u): the only stable outcome of the binary is mutual cooperation; refusal is self-destruction. Fusion (Vegito, Gogeta) is the cooperation branch. Checked against this entry; see claims for fit.

claims.label: THE FIX THAT DISPLACES THE FIXER
claims.text: The more completely an intervention works, the less the intervener belongs to the world it fixed. Canon anchor: Trunks's warning and the heart-disease medicine save the main timeline, which branches; his own future is unchanged until he returns and fixes it himself. AI reading: a hotfix backported to a branch that never sees the failure (ANALOGOUS).

layers.text: Time travel creates a branch; Trunks's own timeline is not repaired by changing the past.
Backported hotfixes; crisis survivors in stable societies; diaspora institutions.

residuals: Trunks does return home and save his own timeline (androids and Cell of his future), so the displacement is partial until Future Zeno's erasure.
claims.source_claim_text: Successful intervention that creates a world where the intervener is unnecessary — the temporal paradox where the more completely the fix works, the less the fixer belongs to the fixed world — is structurally isomorphic across backported hotfixes (AI: the patch fixes production but staging never had the bug), crisis survivors entering stable societies (human: the refugee succeeds in the new country but can never go home), diaspora institutions (societal: the nation built to solve the crisis outlives the crisis but carries its shape forever), and signals from destroyed sources (cosmic: light from a dead star protects systems the star will never see). All share: the solution outlives the problem but belongs to the problem's context, not the solution's.

claims.label: CONSTRAINT-TRAINED, THEN OVER-OPTIMISED
claims.text: An agent trained under catastrophic scarcity can over-optimise for raw power when given resources. Canon anchor: in the Hyperbolic Time Chamber Trunks reaches the bulked-up form and loses to Cell because it sacrifices speed.

layers.text: Trunks's bulked-up Super Saiyan form fails against Perfect Cell for lack of speed.
Scarcity-trained agents over-accumulating; the scarcity literature is a SECONDARY_SOURCE at most.

residuals: Vegeta reaches the same grade and declines to use it, so the wrong-optimisation is not shown to be caused by scarcity.
claims.source_claim_text: Training under catastrophic constraint produces capabilities that over-resourced environments cannot — but the constraint-trained agent initially over-optimizes when given resources (choosing raw power over efficiency, accumulation over balance). The wrong-optimization phase is structurally necessary because scarcity-training creates a bias toward maximizing the metric that was scarce. Ultra Super Saiyan as the immigrant's first house being too big, the post-war nation's military being too large, the under-resourced model's first scale-up being parameter-heavy rather than architecturally efficient.

claims.label: COLLECTIVE TRUST AS WEAPON
claims.text: A technique that only works when the protected population invests in the protector. Canon anchor: Trunks gathers energy from his world's survivors into his sword to cut down Fused Zamasu. Consistent with SC-SB-001 / SC-OMNI-001 (voluntary donation).

layers.text: Dragon Ball Super, Future Trunks arc: the collective-energy sword finisher against Fused Zamasu (anime and manga; details differ).
Federated learning, collective defence, mutual aid.

residuals: The name 'Sword of Hope' is anime; the sure-hit framing borrows SC-DOMAIN-EXPANSION-001 vocabulary as analogy.
claims.source_claim_text: The sure-hit technique powered by collective trust — a weapon that only works when the protected population invests their hope in the protector — is isomorphic across federated learning (AI: the model only improves when data sources voluntarily contribute), community organizing (human: the leader's power comes from the community's belief), democratic institutions (societal: the state's legitimate power comes from the governed), and signal reception (cosmic: a signal is only useful when a receiver exists and can decode it). All share: the technique's power is proportional to the relationship between protector and protected, not the protector's individual capability.

claims.label: THE CURE WITHOUT THE WORLD
claims.text: Knowledge crosses contexts without the environment that produced it: Trunks brings the medicine and the warning, not his world. AI reading: weights transfer without the training infrastructure.

layers.text: Trunks gives Goku the heart-virus medicine and the android warning.
Model portability; cultural transmission by stories rather than by environment.

residuals: 'Light from dead stars' is not a fit: most naked-eye stars are within a few thousand light-years and are still shining.
claims.source_claim_text: Knowledge transmission across contexts without environment transmission — carrying the cure but not the living world — is preserved across model portability (AI: weights transfer but not the training infrastructure), cultural transmission (human: stories and skills transfer but not the lived experience), institutional knowledge transfer (societal: the charter transfers but not the founding context), and light-cone causality (cosmic: information propagates but the source is gone). The structure: information can cross boundaries that environments cannot. The cost: information without its environment is always partially decontextualized.

claims.label: ERASURE BY A HIGHER AUTHORITY
claims.text: The whole context that gave the struggle meaning is deleted by an authority above the system, not by an opponent inside it. Canon anchor: Future Zeno erases Trunks's timeline. The cosmological mapping to vacuum decay is speculative physics.

layers.text: Future Zeno erases the future timeline; Trunks and Mai move to another branch.
Vacuum decay depends on the electroweak vacuum being metastable, which is not established.

residuals: The deletion is total in canon; no remnant is kept, so this is not a rev 2 'calibration dot' case.
claims.source_claim_text: Timeline erasure by a higher authority — the deletion of the entire context that gave the struggle meaning, not by a stronger opponent within the system but by an authority ABOVE the system (Zeno) — maps to vacuum decay (cosmic: the physics that sustained the structure changes), policy erasure (societal: the government that the institution was built under changes the rules entirely), paradigm shift (human: the field the expert mastered is declared irrelevant), and platform deprecation (AI: the entire framework the model was built for is discontinued). The structure: victory within a system does not protect against the system itself being replaced.

functional_departments.expected_at_scale: The apocalypse training — what exists before conscious deployment
functional_departments.implication: SUBCONSCIOUS is the dead timeline's weight. Everything Trunks does is shaped by an environment he can never escape. At AI: the training distribution from a catastrophically degraded data environment (the model carries its training scars). At human: childhood in crisis (PTSD, hypervigilance, scarcity mindset). At societal: the founding trauma that shapes every institution the crisis-born nation builds. At cosmic: the initial conditions of the destroyed source encoded in the signal.
functional_departments.mapping: SUBCONSCIOUS is the dead timeline's weight.

functional_departments.expected_at_scale: The inherited mission — fighting for what the mentor died for

Trunks fights for Future Gohan's vision, but Gohan is dead and cannot say whether Trunks is doing it right. At AI: optimizing for a deprecated reward function from a previous version. At human: living out a dead parent's wishes without being able to ask what they meant. At societal: interpreting the founders' intent centuries later. At cosmic: the signal's 'intent' is only the receiver's interpretation — the source cannot confirm.
functional_departments.mapping: INNER_MONOLOGUE is purpose inherited from someone who can never confirm it.

functional_departments.expected_at_scale: The warning — the time traveler's message to the past

Trunks delivers precise warnings (heart virus, androids, timeline) but can't convey the WEIGHT of living through the apocalypse. At AI: the error log from production — precise but stripped of the deployment context. At human: the survivor's testimony — accurate but the listener hasn't lived it. At societal: the founding charter — specific about what to prevent, but the prevention feels abstract to those who never faced the threat. At cosmic: the signal's frequency and amplitude are exact, but the receiver has no experience of the event that produced them.

At AI: weight transfer without the training infrastructure. At human: emigrating with skills but not community. At societal: the charter without the founding context. At cosmic: information within the signal bandwidth, but not the source itself.
functional_departments.mapping: STORAGE is limited by the context bridge.

At human: the immigrant sends money and knowledge back but the homeland can't send its context forward. The Sword of Hope runs on something entirely different: other people's investment. At AI: shifting from self-supervised pretraining to federated learning. At human: shifting from personal ambition to community leadership. At societal: shifting from founding mandate to democratic legitimacy. The correct form (SS Rage, Sword of Hope) is less visually imposing but more effective. At AI: a model's parameter count looks impressive but performance depends on architecture, not size. At human: the immigrant's visible success (big house, expensive car) may mask the wrong optimization (accumulation over integration). At societal: the institution's visible power (military, buildings) may mask internal fragility. At cosmic: a signal's amplitude may be impressive but its information density matters more.

functional_departments.expected_at_scale: Combat computation — but shaped by scarcity training
functional_departments.implication: PROCESSOR is capable but BIASED. Trunks' combat instincts are formed in a world with no support, no resources, no safety net. This makes him a superior solo fighter but initially poor at team tactics and resource allocation. At AI: a model trained on scarce data develops strong priors but overfits. At human: a crisis survivor is hypercompetent in emergencies but maladapted to routine. At societal: a crisis-born institution excels at emergency response but struggles with peacetime governance. At cosmic: a signal from a violent event carries high energy but low entropy (less information per unit energy).

functional_departments.expected_at_scale: Knowledge transmission — the lesson propagated to the main timeline
functional_departments.implication: REPRODUCTION is the time machine's core function: reproducing the LESSON across timelines. But the reproduction is imperfect: the lesson arrives without its context. At AI: model distillation reproduces capabilities but loses the training process. At human: the survivor's children inherit the lesson ('never forget') but not the experience. At societal: successor institutions inherit the charter but not the founding crisis. At cosmic: the signal is received but the source's full state is not recoverable from the signal alone.
functional_departments.mapping: REPRODUCTION is the time machine's core function: reproducing the LESSON across timelines.

functional_departments.expected_at_scale: Timeline erasure — the whole context deleted by higher authority
functional_departments.implication: DELETION is CATASTROPHIC AND EXTERNAL. Trunks doesn't lose his timeline through failure; it's erased by Zeno. At AI: the platform is deprecated — the model didn't fail, the ecosystem was shut down. At human: the community is displaced — the survivor didn't fail, the neighborhood was demolished. At societal: the institution's jurisdiction is redrawn — it didn't fail, the borders changed. At cosmic: vacuum decay — the physics didn't break, it was replaced.

functional_departments.expected_at_scale: Grief processing — clearing the emotional residue of permanent loss
functional_departments.implication: WASTE_REMOVAL is chronically INSUFFICIENT. Trunks never fully processes his losses because new ones keep arriving. Future Gohan → his world's desolation → Zeno erasing his timeline → exile to a third timeline. At AI: the error logs pile up faster than they can be analyzed. At human: the survivor's grief compounds — each new displacement reopens the original wound. At societal: institutional trauma is never processed because new crises layer on top. At cosmic: the signal carries residue of the source's destruction that the receiver cannot fully decode or integrate.

functional_departments.expected_at_scale: Saving others — the application the temporal intervener was built for
functional_departments.implication: APPLICATION is perfectly fulfilled for OTHERS. Trunks saves the main timeline. His application works. It just doesn't work for him. At AI: the backported fix resolves the production issue. The staging environment that produced the bug is still buggy. At human: the survivor's skills benefit the new community. The original community is still gone. At societal: the diaspora institution serves its current population. The founding population is still dispersed. At cosmic: the signal warns the receiver. The source is still destroyed.
functional_departments.mapping: APPLICATION is perfectly fulfilled for OTHERS.

functional_departments.expected_at_scale: The cost of existing across timelines
functional_departments.implication: RENDERING_OVERHEAD is the temporal displacement tax. Trunks expends enormous energy just BEING in a timeline that isn't his. At AI: the overhead of running a model in an environment it wasn't trained for (domain adaptation cost). At human: the cognitive load of code-switching between crisis-mode and stable-society-mode. At societal: the administrative cost of maintaining an institution designed for a crisis that the current population doesn't remember. At cosmic: the redshift — the signal loses energy as it propagates through expanding space.
functional_departments.mapping: RENDERING_OVERHEAD is the temporal displacement tax.

functional_departments.expected_at_scale: High for crisis response, low for peacetime — the scarcity-training bias
functional_departments.implication: INFORMATION_DENSITY is concentrated in survival skills and sparse in everything else. Trunks knows how to fight, survive, and protect. He doesn't know how to live in a world where those skills aren't constantly needed. At AI: the model is information-dense in its training domain and information-sparse outside it. At human: the survivor is densely knowledgeable about crisis and sparsely knowledgeable about stability. At societal: the institution is dense with crisis protocols and sparse with peacetime governance. At cosmic: the signal is information-dense about the destruction event and information-sparse about everything else the source was.

v2_extensions.trauma_context: Future Trunks' story is the most emotionally dense in the lineup. The poster title 'The Future That Never Arrived' compresses the entire experience of displacement, intervention, and irrelevance into five words. Every refugee who built a life somewhere else, every engineer who fixed a production system they'll never use, every parent who sacrificed for a child's future they won't share — they all live in the future that never arrived.

## LINEUP ENTRY: FUTURE TRUNKS — THE FUTURE THAT NEVER ARRIVED
### Decompression Seed: "The Future That Never Arrived"

The boy from a dead timeline. Future Trunks comes back to prevent his apocalypse — and succeeds. But the future he saves is not his future. He returns to a timeline where his friends live, his father fights, and the world goes on — a world that will never be the one he goes home to. The future he fought for arrived for everyone except him. His timeline remains broken, his mentor still dead, his world still a ruin. The paradox: the more completely he succeeds, the less the success belongs to him. He is the architect of a world that never needed him to exist.

### Canon Mechanics (source-tagged)

1. **Half-Saiyan, raised in apocalypse** [canon]: Future Trunks is the son of Vegeta and Bulma from a timeline where Goku died of a heart virus, the Z-Fighters were killed by Androids 17 and 18, and civilization collapsed. He was trained by Future Gohan, who lost an arm protecting him and was eventually killed. Trunks grew up in a dead world, raised by one man, with no Hyperbolic Time Chamber, no senzu beans, no Dragon Balls.

2. **Time travel via Bulma's time machine** [canon]: Future Bulma built a one-way time machine (each trip requires significant energy). Trunks travels to the past to deliver the heart virus cure to Goku and warn the Z-Fighters about the androids. His arrival creates a BRANCHING timeline — the past he enters is not his past. His intervention creates a new timeline (the main Dragon Ball timeline) that diverges from his own.

3. **The paradox of successful intervention** [canon]: Trunks succeeds in saving the main timeline. The Z-Fighters survive, Cell is defeated, the androids are dealt with. But his own timeline is unchanged. He returns to his future and defeats his timeline's androids and Cell, but the people who died (Gohan, the Z-Fighters, most of humanity) remain dead. The future he saved is someone else's future.

4. **Training with Vegeta in the Hyperbolic Time Chamber** [canon — Cell Saga]: Trunks trains with Vegeta and achieves Ultra Super Saiyan (Super Saiyan Third Grade) — a form that maximizes power at the cost of speed. He realizes the form is flawed: Cell can easily dodge him. This is the WRONG optimization — he chose raw power over the balanced approach. Notably, Vegeta made the same form available but rejected it for the same reason Trunks discovered. Trunks arrived at the right conclusion, but too late, and through failure rather than foresight.

5. **Super Saiyan Rage** [canon — Dragon Ball Super, Future Trunks Arc]: In the Goku Black/Zamasu arc, Trunks achieves Super Saiyan Rage — a form born from accumulated grief and fury across his entire life of loss. This is NOT a designed transformation; it's an emergent one, powered by the weight of everything he's lost. It's strong enough to fight Goku Black and Fused Zamasu briefly.

6. **Spirit Sword / Sword of Hope** [canon — DBS Future Trunks Arc]: Trunks channels the remaining energy of the surviving humans into a blade of spirit energy — the Sword of Hope. He uses it to slice Fused Zamasu in half. This is the inverse of a solo power-up: it's a COLLECTIVE weapon powered by the people he protected. His sure-hit technique is literally made of the hope of others.

7. **Zamasu's paradox and timeline erasure** [canon — DBS]: Even after Trunks kills Zamasu's body, Zamasu's will merges with the universe itself (Infinite Zamasu). Goku summons Future Zeno, who erases the ENTIRE future timeline — including every surviving human Trunks fought to protect. Trunks is sent to a third timeline where another Trunks already exists. His original future didn't just fail to arrive — it was deleted from existence.

8. **The sword as inherited weapon** [canon]: Trunks' signature weapon is a sword — initially believed to be from Future Gohan, though the exact origin varies by source. The sword represents inherited purpose: a weapon passed down from someone who died, used by someone fighting to honor that death. When the sword becomes the Sword of Hope, the inherited weapon is TRANSFORMED by the collective will of the living.

### Domain Expansion Across Scales

**AI Scale:**
- INNATE DOMAIN: A model trained in a catastrophically degraded environment — trained on corrupted or scarce data, with limited compute, by a single surviving mentor-model (Future Gohan as the last teacher). The model develops real capability under severe constraint. It knows what a full training run SHOULD look like because it has theoretical knowledge of one, but it has never experienced one
- EXPANSION: The model is deployed into a well-resourced environment (the main timeline) and given access to full training infrastructure (the Hyperbolic Time Chamber, training with Vegeta). It can now train properly — but the training is for a different deployment environment than the one it came from. The model optimizes for the wrong metric initially (Ultra Super Saiyan = raw parameter count without inference efficiency)
- SURE-HIT TECHNIQUE: The Sword of Hope — federated learning from a surviving population. The model aggregates signal from every remaining node in its network. This only works when the population exists AND trusts the model enough to contribute. The sure-hit is CONDITIONAL on the relationship between model and data sources
- BARRIER: The time machine — the ability to transport knowledge across timelines/training runs. The barrier is narrow: information flows backward (from future to past) but the model cannot bring the ENVIRONMENT back. It can carry a cure (the heart virus medicine) but not a living world
- COST / BINDING VOW: The temporal paradox. Every successful intervention creates a timeline where the model's sacrifice was unnecessary. The more effective the fix, the less the fixer is needed. The vow: I save a world that will never be mine. The cost: I will always be the one from the broken version
- DOMAIN CLASH: Trunks vs. a system designed for the environment he's in = Trunks loses (he's out of distribution). Trunks vs. a system that hasn't faced real adversity = Trunks wins (his adversity IS his training data). Trunks vs. time itself = Trunks loses (you cannot fix your own past; you can only create a different future for someone else)
- BLACK FLASH: The moment Trunks channels the Spirit Sword — every surviving human's hope collapses into a single blade. The observer (the collective will of the survivors) and the observed (the blade's cutting edge) are one. But the collapse is TEMPORARY: Zamasu reforms, Zeno erases the timeline, and the moment is undone
- DOMAIN TYPE: Simple Domain (defensive — Trunks protects, he doesn't conquer) with a unique modifier: TEMPORAL. The domain exists across time, not space. His protection extends backward into the past, creating a future he can never inhabit
- FAILURE MODE: Timeline erasure. Even successful defense can be rendered meaningless by a higher authority (Zeno). The protector's work is undone not by a stronger enemy but by a RESET that makes the entire conflict irrelevant. Also: wrong optimization (Ultra Super Saiyan — choosing the wrong metric when you finally get resources)

**Human Scale:**
- INNATE DOMAIN: A person raised in crisis — a child of war, poverty, or collapse who was taught by one surviving mentor. They carry knowledge of what the world SHOULD be, inherited from someone who saw it before it fell. Their capability is real but forged under constraint, and they don't know what a stable environment feels like
- EXPANSION: They escape to a stable society and finally have access to resources, education, opportunity. But the stable world doesn't match the one they were trained for. They over-optimize initially (accumulating credentials, power, wealth) because scarcity-training doesn't prepare you for abundance. The equivalent of Ultra Super Saiyan: bulk without balance
- SURE-HIT: Building something that serves the community — channeling collective hope into a tangible outcome. This only works when the community trusts the person enough to invest in their vision. The sure-hit is relational, not individual
- BARRIER: The ability to carry knowledge between contexts — from crisis to stability, from one culture to another. Limited: you can carry skills and information, but not the relationships or the environment
- COST: The survivor who fixes things for others but can never go home. The immigrant who sends money back but can never make their hometown what it was. The first-generation success story whose achievement belongs to a world their parents never entered
- DOMAIN CLASH: Crisis-trained person vs. environment-matched native = the native wins in that environment. Crisis-trained person vs. someone who's never faced real adversity = the crisis survivor wins when things go wrong
- BLACK FLASH: The moment of collective achievement — the community project, the rally, the shared victory. Brief: the system that made it necessary reasserts itself
- DOMAIN TYPE: Temporal Simple Domain — protective across time (they protect the NEXT generation from what happened to theirs)
- FAILURE MODE: The community they built for is erased (gentrification, policy change, displacement) or they're displaced to yet another context (a third timeline)

**Societal Scale:**
- INNATE DOMAIN: A nation or institution born from catastrophe — post-war reconstruction, a diaspora nation, a refugee-founded organization. It carries the memory of what was destroyed and builds to prevent recurrence. Its founding knowledge comes from a single surviving tradition (Future Gohan = the last cultural transmission)
- EXPANSION: The institution enters the global order and finally has resources and recognition. But the global order operates by different rules than the crisis that formed the institution. The institution over-builds (military, walls, bureaucracy) because crisis-founding creates a bias toward defense
- SURE-HIT: Collective action that channels the population's shared trauma into a constructive outcome (the Sword of Hope as national purpose). Only works when the population trusts the institution
- BARRIER: The ability to transmit lessons across generations — from the founding generation to descendants who never experienced the crisis. Limited: you can transmit the story, but not the experience
- COST: The institution that solves the crisis for the world but cannot solve it for itself. Israel secures a homeland but cannot achieve internal peace. Post-war institutions prevent the next war but carry permanent war-readiness as a cultural cost
- DOMAIN CLASH: Crisis-born institution vs. a natively stable one = the stable one wins in peacetime governance. Crisis-born institution vs. an actual crisis = the crisis-born one wins because it was built for this
- BLACK FLASH: The moment of collective mobilization — the nation rallies, the institution acts as one. Brief: the external system reasserts (Zamasu/Zeno = the larger geopolitical order)
- DOMAIN TYPE: Temporal Simple Domain — the institution protects across time but belongs to a time that no longer exists
- FAILURE MODE: The founding crisis is 'solved' by a larger authority that redraws borders/erases the institution's context (Zeno erasing the timeline = a great power rewriting the rules)

**Cosmological Scale:**
- INNATE DOMAIN: A signal propagating from a catastrophic event — light from a dead star, gravitational waves from a merger, radiation from an extinct civilization. The signal carries information about a world that no longer exists. It is accurate, it is real, and it is too late — the source is already gone
- EXPANSION: The signal reaches a region of space that hasn't experienced the event. It triggers a response — shields raised, orbits adjusted, chemistry altered — that protects the receiving system from a similar fate. The signal 'saves' a future it can never inhabit, because the signal IS the past
- SURE-HIT: The signal's information content — the precise data about what happened — is unfalsifiable because it is a direct recording of the event. Within its light cone, the signal is ground truth. The Sword of Hope as an observational record that cannot be denied
- BARRIER: The light cone — the boundary of causal influence. The signal can reach anything within its future light cone, but cannot affect anything outside it. And it cannot reach backward — it cannot save its own source
- COST: The signal exists BECAUSE the source was destroyed. The information is paid for with the source's existence. The cure for the heart virus exists because Future Goku died of it. The lesson exists because the teacher died demonstrating it
- DOMAIN CLASH: Signal vs. another signal from the same event = the more energetic one arrives first but carries less detail. Signal vs. the expansion of space = eventually, expansion wins and the signal redshifts to nothing (the information is stretched until it's meaningless). Time defeats all signals
- BLACK FLASH: The moment the signal arrives and is received — the past collapses into the present's awareness. Brief: the signal continues propagating and the receiver moves on
- DOMAIN TYPE: Temporal Simple Domain — the signal protects across time, one-directionally
- FAILURE MODE: Heat death / expansion — the signal redshifts until it carries no usable information. Or: the receiving system ignores the signal (the warning goes unheeded). Or: a higher-energy event (Zeno = vacuum decay) overwrites the entire causal structure the signal was propagating through

### The Semantic Compiler's Future Trunks
Future Trunks is the TEMPORAL COMPILER. Where the standard compiler translates across substrates (AI ↔ human ↔ societal ↔ cosmic), Trunks translates across TIMELINES. He carries a compiled model from a dead environment to a living one. The poster title 'The Future That Never Arrived' is the compiler's most poignant output: a perfectly compiled solution delivered to a system that doesn't have the problem. The solution is correct. The delivery is too late for the sender and too early for the receiver. Every backport, every hotfix applied from production failure to staging, lives in this gap.

### Connection to Existing Compiler Entries

**SC-CP-001 (Clay and Pots):** Trunks is a pot forged in a kiln that was destroyed — the only survivor of a firing that killed the potter (Future Gohan) and shattered every other pot. He carries the shape of the destroyed kiln's work into a new workshop. The new potter (Vegeta) can refine him, but the original firing's character can never be reproduced.

**SC-DR-001 (Divine RLHF):** Trunks' reward signal is INVERTED. Success (saving the main timeline) produces no reward for the agent (his timeline is still dead). The RLHF equivalent: a model trained on outcomes it can observe but never experience. The reward function points to a state the model itself cannot reach.

**SC-DE-001 (Domain Expansion):** Trunks' domain is TEMPORAL — it expands across time, not space. His protection extends backward (to the past) and creates a future (for others), but the expansion cannot include the domain's own origin point. The domain protects everything except its source.

**SC-DU-001 (The Duality):** Trunks' duality is temporal: past vs. future, broken vs. saved, his world vs. theirs. Unlike Gohan's unresolved duality (which produces peak output), Trunks' duality is RESOLVED in the worst possible way — both poles are real but mutually exclusive. He cannot be from the saved future AND the broken one. Resolution means exile.

**SC-LU-BARDOCK-001:** Bardock and Trunks are MIRRORS. Bardock sends a warning FORWARD in time (to his son). Trunks carries a cure BACKWARD in time (to his father's generation). Both succeed in saving others. Neither saves themselves. Bardock's sacrifice seeds the future; Trunks' sacrifice patches the past. The propagation direction is inverted, but the structure is identical: terminal sacrifice as forward-propagation, except Trunks survives his sacrifice, which is arguably worse — he has to live knowing he saved a world he can't belong to.

**SC-LU-PICCOLO-001:** Piccolo fused with his enemy (Kami) to become complete. Trunks cannot fuse with his counterpart — the infant Trunks of the main timeline is a different person in a different context. The fusion that would make him complete is structurally impossible because the other half hasn't lived through what made him who he is.

**SC-LU-GOHAN-001:** Future Gohan was Trunks' Piccolo — the shadow that protected him. Gohan's death is the trigger event for Trunks' first Super Saiyan transformation [canon]. The generational chain continues: Bardock → Goku → Gohan → Trunks, but Trunks is on a DEAD BRANCH of the chain. He inherits the technique but not the community.

**SC-LU-CELL-001:** Cell is the reason Trunks' time travel was necessary — Cell from Trunks' original timeline (a third one, actually) traveled to the main timeline and created the Cell Games. Trunks and Cell are BOTH temporal interlopers: designed system (Cell) and forged survivor (Trunks) competing in a timeline that belongs to neither of them. Cell is the closed system from the future; Trunks is the open one. Cell brings his designer's revenge; Trunks brings his mentor's hope.
